text:
sam: noticing a spike of 502/504s from hosted-api around 21:04 UTC, majority coming from /v1/generate, customers reporting timeouts
support-bot: alert posted: hosted-api 502-rate exceeded threshold (21:04 UTC)
elyse: thanks — collecting logs and repro steps. symptoms: high 95p latency (>10s), many upstream `connect error` from gateway, and app-level KV timeouts to prefix cache
sam: gateway snippet: ```[2026-03-17T21:04:12Z] upstream connect error or disconnect while reading response header from upstream, client=10.8.2.11, request="POST /v1/generate"```
raj: oncall here. can you paste the cache errors from the app side?
elyse: app logs: ```ERROR kv/prefix: redis read timeout, conn=10.2.3.14:6379, err="i/o timeout"
WARN kv/prefix: closed connection while waiting for reply``` also seeing `ERR maxclients` in redis logs around the same time
beth: infra metrics show eviction spike and master repl lag -> looks like leader election churned at 21:02-21:05, a bunch of clients reconnected and hit connection limits
sam: any recent deploy that touches cache config?
elyse: nope, no config deploy. but there was a large batch embedding job from customer X starting ~21:00 that opened many concurrent prefix reads (likely caching lookup storm)
support-ian: contacted customer X, asked them to throttle their batch jobs temporarily. raising priority ticket to infra to mitigate now
raj: starting mitigation: scaling redis read replicas + bumping `maxclients` on master; also initiating a controlled rolling restart of the cluster to clear unhealthy conns. switching API read path to memcached fallback for prefix-read keys: `infra cache switch --prefix-vhost=hosted-api --pattern=responses --to=memcached-fallback`
sam: after switching to fallback we saw 502s drop substantially, but there are still intermittent 504s while connection pools warm up — looking into pool sizing/timeout defaults
elyse: quick repro that we used for customer: `curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"redwood-2","prompt":"hi"}'` -> request hangs ~10s then gateway returns 502
oncall-sre: metrics: connection drops to redis master peaked at 21:03, rolling restart completed by 21:10 and error rate decayed to baseline ~21:15. repl-backlog pressure and client connection churn line up with customer X's job start time
beth: preliminary root cause: sudden client-side burst opened too many persistent connections to the redis master, master hit `maxclients` -> new conns refused and many existing conns got dropped -> app experienced KV timeouts -> gateway surfaced 502/504 upstream errors. short-term mitigations: apply fallback to memcached, throttle large customers, bump `maxclients`, and restart cluster. long-term: enforce connection pooling/circuit breakers at API layer and autoscale cache tier based on active connections, improve prefix cache eviction policies
support-ian: I've updated customer X and asked them to limit concurrent workers to 10 for now. opened INC-20260317-01 for tracking and postmortem
sam: moving the full RCA to #postmortems once we have logs and timelines. tagging @eng-infra and @eng-sre for follow-up action items
raj: will post the infra diffs (autoscale rules + memcached fallback playbook) and a PR to add circuit-breaker + backoff on prefix lookup in the API client
elyse: :thumbsup:
